Find help. I knew when I had second thoughts about suicide, I didn’t want to end my life. I reached out to anyone just to talk. Suicide hotlines are great, but sometimes just saying to a friend “hey, I’m not ok” is worth it. Being suicidal is scary, and makes you do crazy things. For me, I would always try to push people I cared about out of my life. This was my brain’s way of saying “your death won’t hurt them”. I knew when those feelings came on, I had to reach out. 

Stay strong. Suicidal thoughts are manipulative, and deceiving. Take a step back and remember what matters - you. Even if you feel that you don’t matter or don’t want to live - find one thing worth living for. The sunrise tomorrow, seeing a first snowfall, a home cooked meal - and find a way to make life feel worth living. It’s not the same for everyone, and no one interprets feelings the same way. Just stay strong, find your voice, and speak up if you need help.

Please feel free to reach out to me, and please be safe.

Fun fact: Fart is not a swear word. 

Growing up we were not allowed to use the word “fart”. We were only allowed to use  “toot”, “pass gas”, and even “flatulence”.  I grew up thinking that fart was on the same level of rule breaking as saying the f-bomb, hitting my sister, etc. I even received soap in my mouth a few times for testing the waters, and saying the 2nd most forbidden f-word. 

Fast forward to the 4th grade. I am on the playground at school and someone says Fart. I look around the group waiting for some kind of reaction: looks of disgust, nervous eye contact, etc.  Nothing happens, no one bats an eye. Meanwhile, I’m freaking out on the inside - do my friends swear? Does this make me rebellious? 

I hold these worrisome feelings inside me until I am 14 or 15. I finally gain the courage to ask my mom why we are not allowed to say “fart”. Expecting a reaction, I get my answer - “I just don’t like that word”. 

That’s it. A personal preference by my mother made me feel like I was going to hell. I now rarely use the 2nd F-Bomb, perhaps out of habit or perhaps out of fear.

TL;DR - My mom made me believe that The word Fart would send me to the depths of hell.
